purpose: A research-only thematic radar for Power Stack. It is not a portfolio view and does not mechanically change company fundamental scores. The canonical base stores durable economic mechanisms; faster daily overlays, Cranium work and Live Desk intake may change attention and rank, but require independent verification before becoming canonical evidence.

environment.label: Restrictive, inflation-sensitive risk-on with strong physical capex but fragile financial duration
environment.summary: The dominant regime is no longer simply Fed-hike risk. Long-end nominal and real yields, term premium, credit conditions and competition for capital can stay restrictive even if the Fed holds. At the same time, physical AI, grid and energy-scarcity capex remains real, creating unusually wide dispersion between funded cash-generative infrastructure and leverage-dependent duration.

promoteWhen: A material catalyst changes the mechanism, timing, investability or beneficiary set of a thesis
At least two independent research streams converge, with preference for primary or official evidence
The theme has a clear next test that can strengthen or invalidate it
parkWhen: The thesis remains structurally valid but nothing material has changed
The theme duplicates a broader active mechanism
The signal is mostly valuation excitement, positioning or narrative without improving commercial evidence
A more recent cross-asset mechanism has materially higher significance
evidenceHierarchy: Primary company filings, company releases, regulators, central banks, government and official data
Persisted Power Stack research and verified dossier outputs
Cranium, sell-side PDFs, positioning notes and creator transcripts as hypothesis inputs only unless independently corroborated

methodology.recencyRule: Use the last 14 days as the sweep window, with substantially heavier weight on the most recent four days. Older evidence supports or contradicts the current mechanism but should not automatically outrank fresh evidence.
methodology.ratesRule: Do not use one global high-rates/low-rates flag. For US/global assets separate refinancing/funding sensitivity, customer-financing sensitivity, capex/cash-flow sensitivity and valuation/discount-rate sensitivity. For China distinguish low funding rates from weak credit demand and poor transmission.
methodology.aiFundingRule: Funded backlog is more valuable than announced capacity; contracted cash flow is more valuable than proposed megawatts; equipment and infrastructure sellers with visible orders are preferred to speculative project owners dependent on future financing.
methodology.portfolioGuardrail: Theme rank changes research priority, action thresholds and required margin of safety. It does not mechanically change Base Conviction or holdings fundamental scores.

regimeModifiers.name: Low Volatility / Thin Protection Fragility
regimeModifiers.summary: Calm index volatility can coexist with violent theme and factor dispersion when positioning is crowded, short covering is heavy and put protection is thin. Treat VIX, MOVE, skew, put demand and weak-credit spreads as confirmation tools rather than a standalone directional signal.

themes.name: Rates Ambiguity + Long-End Funding Stress
themes.status: Active macro regime / highest cross-asset impact
themes.summary: Long-end nominal and real yields, term premium, credit spreads and funding availability are now first-order operating variables for capital-intensive themes. A Fed hold is not automatically easier financial conditions if the 10- to 30-year curve and real yields remain restrictive.
themes.whyDeveloping: By the latest official US cash close on September 4, Treasury yields were roughly 4.37% at 2 years, 4.78% at 10 years and 5.24% at 30 years. Stronger August labour and services evidence kept near-term policy uncertainty alive while fiscal supply, energy inflation and global duration pressure kept the long end restrictive. The analytical question has shifted from simply 'will the Fed hike?' to 'what is the all-in cost and availability of capital after the decision?'
themes.nextTest: September 10 PPI, September 11 CPI and the September 15-16 FOMC, with emphasis on the post-event 10Y/30Y/real-yield and credit response rather than the policy headline alone.
themes.invalidation: Sustained easing in long-end nominal and real yields, credit spreads and funding conditions that materially lowers hurdle rates for capital-intensive growth.
sourceClasses: Cranium synthesis corroborated by official data

mainNews.title: US Treasury daily yield curve remains restrictive into September event risk
mainNews.implication: The long end remains restrictive enough to matter for discount rates and project economics before the September FOMC.

mainNews.title: September inflation and FOMC calendar creates a dense rates repricing window
mainNews.implication: PPI, CPI and the FOMC can rapidly change the ranking, but only if the long end and funding markets confirm the move.

themes.name: Hormuz Energy Stress: Refined Products + Shipping
themes.status: Active geopolitical and inflation transmission theme
themes.summary: The Iran/Hormuz shock is no longer best understood as one crude-oil trade. The sharper transmission is through refined products, tanker availability, insurance, route security, LNG and regional power while crude rerouting can partially adapt.
themes.whyDeveloping: Weekend US-Iran vessel attacks and unusually depressed Hormuz traffic materially increased maritime risk, while OPEC+ maintained October production policy. The market now has to price both immediate physical disruption and the possibility that crude flows adapt faster than diesel, jet, fuel oil, LNG and shipping bottlenecks.
themes.nextTest: September 10 EIA petroleum report, September 11 IEA Oil Market Report and any material change in Hormuz vessel security or Iranian restrictions.
themes.invalidation: Normalised Hormuz traffic plus sustained normalisation in product cracks, freight/insurance and LNG risk premiums rather than crude alone.

mainNews.title: Hormuz traffic drops sharply after US-Iranian vessel attacks
mainNews.implication: Maritime security, freight and insurance have become direct energy-price transmission channels.

mainNews.title: OPEC+ maintains September production requirements for October
mainNews.implication: Producer policy does not currently offset the shipping and product bottleneck through an additional October supply increase.

themes.name: AI Buildout: Power, Grid + Time-to-Power
themes.summary: AI demand remains strong, but scarce physical inputs increasingly sit outside the accelerator: generation, transmission, transformers, substations, switchgear, interconnection, cooling, water and construction capacity. Time-to-power and equipment lead times are becoming more investable than headline AI narratives.
themes.whyDeveloping: Recent research continues to show strong AI-server, electrical-equipment and data-centre demand while the market simultaneously questions the quality of some proposed load. This makes realised orders, backlog, deposits, interconnection progress and power procurement more important than announced megawatts.
themes.nextTest: Supplier order/backlog updates, hyperscaler financing disclosures, data-centre utility interconnection evidence and any cancellation or deposit slippage that reaches equipment backlogs.
themes.invalidation: Broad deterioration in supplier backlog, deposits, utility interconnection commitments and actual funded load rather than isolated project cancellations.

mainNews.title: Texas data-centre review broadens the bottleneck from electricity to full-site infrastructure
mainNews.source: Office of the Governor of Texas / PUCT-ERCOT directive
mainNews.implication: Projects without credible power, water and cooling plans face higher execution risk while scarce enabling equipment gains strategic value.

themes.name: AI Buildout: Financing + Cash Conversion
themes.summary: AI demand and AI project economics can diverge. Cost of capital, funding channel, customer prepayments, guarantees, project finance, converts, debt capacity, utilisation and free-cash-flow conversion now determine which announced projects create equity value.
themes.whyDeveloping: The latest rates and Cranium work shows that higher long-end yields can reduce project equity value even when customer demand remains intact. This broadens the theme from one company's convertible financing into a system-wide diligence lens for utilities, data centres, electrical equipment, semiconductors, automation and pre-revenue nuclear.
themes.nextTest: Any new hyperscaler, utility or data-centre financing disclosure plus the September inflation/FOMC sequence and evidence that funding stress is or is not reaching supplier orders.
themes.invalidation: Broadly falling funding costs with improving cash conversion and sustained backlog quality across capital-intensive AI beneficiaries.
sourceClasses: Cranium and sell-side work used as hypothesis input

mainNews.title: Nebius upsizes convertible financing as data-centre buildout accelerates
mainNews.implication: Strong demand does not remove financing, dilution and cash-conversion risk.

themes.name: Energy Security Rerouting + Asian Demand Destruction
themes.summary: The second leg of the Iran shock is adaptation. Rerouting, alternative crude sourcing, LNG substitution, inventory drawdowns and weaker Asian demand can cap outright crude convexity while still rewarding tankers, strategic corridors, US LNG and selected upstream capacity.
themes.whyDeveloping: The latest evidence increasingly separates immediate disruption from the market's ability to adapt. Crude can find replacement routes and barrels faster than some refined products and gas flows, so beneficiaries and losers are no longer identical to the first-stage oil shock.
themes.nextTest: IEA September OMR and continued vessel/import data showing whether adaptation is reducing the crude shortage faster than product and gas shortages.
themes.invalidation: A renewed physical escalation that overwhelms rerouting capacity, or a rapid full normalisation that removes both scarcity and rerouting economics.
sourceClasses: shipping data reported by high-quality media

mainNews.title: Oil market increasingly balances disruption against rerouting and demand destruction
mainNews.source: Power Stack synthesis from verified energy and shipping data
mainNews.implication: The investable energy hierarchy is shifting from simple crude beta toward logistics, products, LNG and resilient low-cost supply.

themes.name: Copper: Grid Demand vs Inventory Distortion
themes.status: Structural demand theme with cyclical confirmation risk
themes.summary: Grid, transmission and AI-related electrical demand remain structurally copper-intensive, but price signals are distorted by inventory geography, tariff-related stockpiling and weak China credit transmission. The correct trade is not generic copper scarcity; it is scarcity confirmed by end demand and inventory drawdown.
themes.whyDeveloping: The physical AI and grid thesis remains strong enough to keep copper high in the hierarchy, while China's weak domestic transmission prevents a clean broad-demand call. This creates a useful split between structural grid consumption and macro-sensitive China industrial demand.
themes.nextTest: China activity/credit data and evidence that reported inventories begin drawing while grid and electrical-equipment orders remain firm.
themes.invalidation: Persistent inventory accumulation combined with weakening grid, industrial and China demand.

themes.name: China: Balance-Sheet Support + Selective AI/Infrastructure
themes.status: Selective state-supported reflation, not broad demand repair
themes.summary: China's problem is cheap money with weak transmission, not an expensive sovereign funding curve. Fresh state-bank and insurer recapitalisation can improve capacity to lend and invest without proving households or private businesses want to borrow. The better exposures are policy-backed power, grid, industrial automation and confirmed AI infrastructure rather than generic growth beta.
themes.whyDeveloping: August manufacturing PMI improved to 49.8 with new orders above 50, while non-manufacturing activity remained weak. Fresh state financial-sector capital injections strengthen balance sheets but do not yet establish broad credit demand. This upgrades China from a generic fiscal-infrastructure card into a transmission-quality and beneficiary-selection theme.
themes.nextTest: Mid-September China activity and credit data. Promote only if credit transmission, private/new-order breadth and actual strategic capex improve together.
themes.invalidation: Continued weak private credit demand, deteriorating orders and currency stress despite additional balance-sheet support.

mainNews.title: August China PMI shows selective manufacturing improvement but weak broader activity
mainNews.source: National Bureau of Statistics of China
mainNews.implication: Improving manufacturing orders are not yet equivalent to broad domestic reflation.

mainNews.title: China adds fresh capital to major state financial institutions
mainNews.implication: Balance-sheet capacity is improving before there is proof of stronger private credit demand.

themes.name: Food / Fertilizer Affordability + Feedstock Divergence
themes.summary: Fertilizer remains a differentiated trade. North American nitrogen can benefit from comparatively cheap gas and constrained global supply, while phosphate economics can be hurt by sulphur and freight scarcity. The second-order risk is farmer affordability and application cuts rather than simply higher fertilizer prices.
themes.whyDeveloping: Iran/Hormuz shipping and energy stress keeps fertilizer feedstocks and freight relevant, but a stronger dollar, high rates and weak farm economics can destroy end demand. The investment edge remains in producers with advantaged feedstocks and resilient balance sheets rather than generic fertilizer beta.
themes.nextTest: Autumn fertilizer demand, Gulf export recovery, sulphur availability and evidence of farmer application cuts.
themes.invalidation: Normalised fertilizer/feedstock trade with collapsing nitrogen margins and no measurable affordability or application stress.

mainNews.title: CF Industries says global nitrogen supply remains constructive into 2027
mainNews.implication: Cheap North American gas and constrained global nitrogen supply remain a differentiated producer advantage.

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel-Cycle Scarcity
themes.status: Structural fuel-security theme with financing split
themes.summary: Operating nuclear and fuel-cycle scarcity can benefit from energy-security demand while pre-revenue reactor developers remain highly exposed to financing costs and project execution. High rates therefore increase the attractiveness gap between proven fuel/operating assets and speculative project finance.
themes.whyDeveloping: The energy-security shock and AI power demand keep nuclear strategically relevant, while the new capital-sensitivity framework makes project stage decisive. Contracted uranium and operating nuclear cash flows are fundamentally different from pre-revenue SMR equity duration.
themes.nextTest: New utility contracting, enrichment/fuel-cycle evidence and any SMR funding or customer milestone that materially changes financing risk.
themes.invalidation: Weakening fuel contracting and security demand together with improving alternative power availability; for SMRs, inability to secure credible funded customers remains a separate negative gate.

themes.name: Industrial Automation Before Humanoids
themes.status: Commercial automation preferred to speculative robotics duration
themes.summary: High funding costs sharpen the difference between automation already generating customer ROI and humanoid platforms that still require substantial capital and commercialization proof. Prefer deployed warehouse, factory and logistics automation with visible orders, service revenue and payback periods.
themes.whyDeveloping: Current China and global rates conditions make the commercial sequence more important. Cheap local China funding does not guarantee private capex, while expensive global capital raises the hurdle for long-duration robotics. Proven order flow should outrank narrative TAM.
themes.nextTest: Confirmed deployments and backlog conversion, especially for China automation names, versus additional capital raises or delayed customer rollouts.
themes.invalidation: Broad deterioration in industrial automation orders or clear commercial proof that humanoid economics and funding quality have caught up with conventional automation.

themes.name: Gold / Fiscal-Monetary Hedge vs Real Yields
themes.status: Structural hedge with tactical real-yield headwind
themes.summary: Gold remains useful against fiscal, geopolitical and confidence risk, but high real yields and a firm dollar are direct tactical headwinds. The informative signal is whether gold can rise despite restrictive real yields; that would indicate unusually strong non-rate demand.
themes.whyDeveloping: Recent hawkish repricing weakened gold even as geopolitical stress remained elevated, reminding the portfolio that the hedge is not mechanically bullish during every crisis. This makes real-yield interaction the correct trigger rather than geopolitical headlines alone.
themes.nextTest: US PPI/CPI/FOMC and whether bullion can hold or strengthen if real yields remain elevated.
themes.invalidation: Persistent higher real yields and dollar strength accompanied by a decisive breakdown in bullion and miner breadth.

themes.name: Water Scarcity: Food + Power + Freight Collision
themes.status: Structural physical constraint with limited fresh four-day evidence
themes.summary: Water scarcity remains a cross-sector constraint spanning crops, river freight, municipal systems, cooling and power generation. The structural thesis is intact, but it has less fresh evidence and lower immediate catalyst density than rates, Iran, AI and China.
themes.whyDeveloping: August drought evidence remains valid and municipal water-network economics remain investable, but the most recent four-day sweep did not produce a new regime-changing water catalyst. It stays active because the constraint can re-enter quickly through weather, nuclear cooling or crop losses.
themes.nextTest: Updated European river/crop conditions, municipal water order books and any renewed cooling constraints on power generation.
themes.invalidation: Sustained hydrological normalisation combined with weaker water-infrastructure order growth and no material power/crop constraints.

mainNews.title: Europe's deepening drought hits water, crops, shipping and power
mainNews.implication: Water remains a multi-sector operating constraint rather than a standalone environmental theme.

parkedThemes.name: Natural Rubber: Acreage + Labour Squeeze
parkedThemes.reason: The structural acreage/labour thesis remains plausible, but there is insufficient fresh four-day evidence or near-term cross-asset transmission to justify active canonical bandwidth.
parkedThemes.reactivateWhen: Fresh producer pricing/volume evidence, material acreage contraction, weather shock or tire-demand change materially alters the mechanism.

parkedThemes.name: Personalised Oncology / mRNA Optionality
parkedThemes.reason: Event-specific healthcare optionality remains valid but lacks a recent catalyst strong enough to compete with current macro, energy and physical-infrastructure themes.
parkedThemes.reactivateWhen: A material clinical, regulatory, commercial or reimbursement catalyst changes probability-weighted economics.
